note: Lesotho: no employer may employ, and no one who isn't a citizen may accept employment, without a valid work permit from the Director, National Employment Service, who first certifies that no qualified citizen is on the labour market database (Labour Act, 2024, Act 3 of 2024, ss. 161–163, in force on publication in the Gazette Extraordinary No. 22 of 2 April 2024). Its fourth schedule charges M1,000 to apply and M2,000 for a certificate of six months or less, M2,500 up to two years and M3,000 for two years. Section 161(4) says a non-citizen engaged in Lesotho to provide temporary services isn't employed for the section's purposes; the Act gives that no length, so no days are modelled. Read in LesLII's copy of the gazetted Act through archive.org's snapshot of 13 July 2025 (LesLII refuses this client behind a Cloudflare check); no later amendment was found, and the Home Affairs residence permits aren't modelled apart. Read again on 2026-11-03: web.archive.org couldn't be read (web.archive.org reset every connection each time it was tried, and LesLII itself answered with a Cloudflare check), so its reading of 2026-10-31 stands. Until 2026-11-03 LesothoLII's PDF (through archive.org) was cited as primary; it is a legal information institute's copy of the law, so secondary since the ruling of 2026-11-03, so it was relabelled, and the gazette's own pages (Laws.Africa's publication scan of Gazette No. 22) were read that day: s. 1 and s. 161(1) and (4) say what was quoted, so nothing changed.

sources.title: Labour Act, 2024 (Act 3 of 2024), Government Gazette Extraordinary No. 22, 2 April 2024, ss. 1 and 161 (LesLII's copy, archive.org snapshot of 13 July 2025)
sources.said: This Act may be cited as the Labour Act, 2024 and shall come into operation on the date of publication in the Gazette. ... No employer shall employ any person in Lesotho who is not a citizen of Lesotho, and no such person shall accept employment in Lesotho, unless that person is in possession of a valid work permit issued by the Director, National Employment Service. ... a person who is not a citizen of Lesotho, but who is engaged in Lesotho to provide temporary services shall not be considered to be employed or to have accepted employment
